kpi_surface_dispositions.rationale: This KPI trains and evaluates ENTIRELY on OpenPoly's own dielectric-constant column (n=295, scaffold-safe holdout MAE=0.4040 R2=0.5649, LOSO-CV R2=0.6591), which C8's own admissibility control found 0/295 violations under the Frohlich-equivalent OpenPoly-internal check. This file's headline numbers remain citable AS-IS, scoped explicitly to the OpenPoly literature population -- they must not be read as evidence about RadonPy-derived dielectric predictions, and the KPI's own claim_locks already restrict it to 'baseline_valid_on_openpoly_scaffold_distribution_only'.

This KPI evaluates the OpenPoly-trained model against RadonPy's static_dielectric_const as ground truth for n_test_radonpy=1077 rows (reported best_external_R2=0.0248, marginal lift_over_null=0.7001). Because 89.5% of that target column is physically inadmissible (eps_static<n^2), this MAE/R2 pair is evaluated against corrupted labels and is NOT interpretable as an external-validity measurement of dielectric-constant predictive skill until RadonPy's label integrity is repaired (data-acquisition ask already filed by C8 fire 1).

This KPI pools 1077 RadonPy rows (962/1075=89.5% corrupted) with 295 OpenPoly rows for BOTH training and evaluation, reporting overall test R2=0.6991 and RadonPy-slice test R2=0.7001. C8 fire 2 showed this large apparent RadonPy skill is an artifact of the RF exploiting the corrupted majority's low variance near the under-converged electronic-only limit: on the honest, zero-contamination clean-only subset (n=113), the equivalent RF collapses to R2=-0.0263. The 95% conformal PI-coverage guarantee (0.9745) remains a mechanically valid statement about interval calibration on THIS corrupted target, but the accompanying R2/MAE point-skill numbers must not be cited as evidence of real dielectric-constant predictive capability.

C8 fire 1's dielectric row (full-population ML R2=0.6427) is internally superseded by c8_fire3_final_consolidated_receipt.v1.json's dielectric_constant.verdict=NO_COMPETENT_MODEL. Fire 1 remains on disk as prior-fire audit trail; any external citation of its dielectric numbers in isolation (without fire 2/3 context) would be misleading.
